title: Backpressure on ingest pipeline
description:
Return a clean error to senders when the write pipeline is saturated rather than queuing articles unboundedly and exhausting memory.

Why this issue exists:
A fast peer or a flood of POST commands can fill the in-memory staging buffer (the write-ahead staging introduced in the transit WAL epic) faster than Kubo can drain it. Without backpressure, the process grows without bound until OOM. Senders need a clear signal to back off and retry.

Scope:
- Add a configurable high-water mark to the ingest staging buffer (default: 1000 pending articles or 256 MB, whichever is hit first)
- When the high-water mark is exceeded:
  - IHAVE/TAKETHIS: respond 436 (Retry later) per RFC 4644
  - POST: respond 400 with 'server busy, retry later'
- Emit a structured log event and increment a Prometheus counter when backpressure is applied
- Add [ingest] max_pending_articles and max_pending_bytes config fields
- Backpressure is released automatically as the drain catches up; no manual intervention required

Acceptance criteria:
- Sending 2000 articles faster than Kubo can write them triggers 436 responses after the high-water mark
- Prometheus metric ingest_backpressure_total increments on each rejected article
- After Kubo catches up, new articles are accepted again without restart
- Memory usage stays bounded under flood conditions
